name: Sage Grey
lede: Sage Grey is a greyish olive, listed among the greys and named for the sage plant.

sections.title: A grey with some green in it
sections.body:
Paterson defines sage-grey as a greyish olive colour [1]. He lists it in his index of greys, not among the greens [2]. Its neighbor in the dictionary is [[sage-green]], a greener entry [1].

The books say nothing about when the name arrived, and no dye or pigment is attached to it [1]. Paterson also defines olive grey and moss-grey as olive greys, close in sense [1][3]; the plain plant color is [[sage]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 865 hold this color at 5% of the canvas or more, as photographed [4]. The earliest example is María Josefa Sánchez's *Crucifixion* of 1646 [4]. Printed use of *sage grey* peaked in 1912 and has been low and steady since [5]. The match counts any painting with this color covering at least a twentieth of the canvas, so it shows where the color appears in photographs of paintings, not that the painters ever called it by this name.

origin.named_after: the sage plant, by leaf color (the books do not say; origin undocumented)
